events.context: Reading text about a relationship analyzed through legal and technical metaphors, starting with declarations of love and non-love.
Extracting key actions: declarations of 'he doesn't love you' and 'he loves you' with legal terms like legal title and equitable interest.
Noting specific behaviors: audit funding, review HPS, quantify self-pleasure habits, shutdown system without condom, hug at door, go to Yandangshan for via ferrata.
Identifying legal frameworks: Gissing v Gissing and Stack v Dowden used to argue behavior overrides verbal declarations.
Concluding verdict: person cannot reconcile legal title and equitable interest; user holds equitable interest but lacks legal title.
Describing a scenario: after via ferrata, in bed, user initiates kissing, then says 'slow down' to take control.
Outlining Phase 3 term sheet negotiation: user speaks in technical terms (SLA, term, deploy) to redefine relationship, propose platonian friends, compare open relationships.
Analyzing strategic moves: language switch, framework redefinition, valuation reassessment, escape route with background process, performance feedback.
Considering possible responses from him: defensive errors, citing precedent, system shutdown, and user's prepared rebuttals using legal and technical arguments.
Final action: user decides to hug him, let him listen to heartbeat, and say '小树哥哥别错过我' as a fallback position without technical translation.
